business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF statute), Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT regime), Decree 830 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB), Decree 1068 of 2015 as amended, and Article 44 of Law 2155 of 2021, each as amended from time to time.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Full company registry or Companies Office in source country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for local incorporation representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport and/or identity documents of ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent government authority in source country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residency for UBO or parent entity (for DTA evaluation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National tax authority of source country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, European Union restrictive measures list, Colombian national counter-terrorism and organized crime lists, and international PEP databases; enhanced due diligence and beneficial ownership certification under Decree 830 of 2021; continuous (near-real-time) negative news and sanctions re-screening for at least the first five years after incorporation; compliance with UIAF Circulars and FATF Recommendations applicable to Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (operated by Confecámaras; filings submitted through the local Cámara de Comercio, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate legal names must be expressed in Spanish alphabet and Latin characters; non-Spanish names must be phonetically transliterated or adapted into Spanish script; names must comply with connotation and public order restrictions; acronyms are permitted if derived from the full proposed legal name; the registry requires the name to distinguish the entity from any existing trademark or company in the same business or similar activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon notice of name rejection or negative homonym certification, the incorporator may submit a formal administrative appeal ('recurso de reposición y en subsidio apelación') to the relevant Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) business days; the Chamber must resolve the 'reposición' within five (5) business days and may forward 'apelación' to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio for final administrative determination; if still rejected, judicial review may be sought under Law 1437 of 2011 (Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally accepted for low-risk standard MedTech regulatory consulting entities, provided a physical local address is registered with the Chamber of Commerce and the company maintains sufficient operational substance, administrative records, and access to corporate documentation; the Superintendencia de Sociedades may require demonstration of physical capacity upon examination or challenge.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; estimated probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first twelve months of operation is 5–15% for a low-risk, standard-tier consultancy; inspections are more likely if the entity is designated as a DNFBP or registers with financial sector counterparties, but the current commercial profile does not trigger systematic supervisory inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and homonymy certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local chamber of commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation document (private deed) registration fee in the commercial registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on registered capital; minimum tariff applies for SAS with zero capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: DIAN pre-registration and NIT (tax identification number) issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free of charge by statutory mandate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, notarization, and sworn translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document set; consistent with Hague Apostille Convention fee practices

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal counsel for pre-incorporation review, UBO analysis, and drafting of constitutional documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk SAS formation with full AML/CFT diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Articles 1-49) establishing the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada; Colombian Código de Comercio Articles 110, 115, 353-372; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (Registro Único Empresarial y Social - RUES procedure); DIAN Resolución 000165 de 2023 (tax registry RUT and electronic invoicing requirements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Bogotá Chamber of Commerce) operating through the national RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Deed) executed by all founding shareholders and filed with the Chamber of Commerce; a Public Deed (Escritura Pública) is required only if real property is contributed as in-kind capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an S.A.S.; subscribed capital may be paid in installments provided that full disbursement is completed within two years from incorporation. No escrow account is mandated; cash contributions are held in the company's corporate bank account following registration. In-kind contributions must be described and valued in the incorporation document.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. Ratification of Share Subscription. The share capital subscribed by the founding shareholders, as stated in the incorporation document, is ratified in full; each subscribed share is accepted and issued accordingly. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is established in Bogotá D.C., Colombia, at the address stated in the bylaws, hereby adopted as the official domicile for all legal purposes and notifications. 3. Officer Appointments. Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Legal Representative (Presidente) and Mr./Ms. [Name] as Alternate Legal Representative, with full powers under Colombian law. 4. Administrative Authorization. The Legal Representative is authorized to complete the Chamber of Commerce registration, DIAN tax enrollment, bank account opening, and all necessary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá through the RUES online portal (Solicitud de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the RUES web system, submit up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference, and pay the nominal search fee. The system issues a pre-approval certificate (Certificado de Homonimia) valid for 30 days. The name must not coincide with an existing registered entity or a trademark protected under SIC.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (maximum three)
Identification documents of each founding shareholder
Basic corporate purpose summary
Proof of payment of the name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected, the applicant selects an alternative pre-approved name from the submitted list or files a new search and re-attempts registration within the validity window; no substantive penalty applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (only if real property is contributed) or directly before the founding shareholders with legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the company name, corporate purpose (medical device FDA/CE regulatory consulting), registered office, capital structure, share classes and voting rights, term, and bylaws. All shareholders must sign, and signatures must be authenticated before the Chamber of Commerce or a notary when required. The document must state the capital payment schedule.
required_dossiers: Pre-approved name certificate
Shareholders' identification documents
Draft bylaws including corporate governance rules
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Statement of subscribed capital and payment term
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is rejected for inconsistency (e.g., capital payment term exceeding the statutory two-year maximum), the shareholders execute an amended corollary document and refile; legal counsel corrects the clause prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Registration and RUES Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Registration Office) via online RUES filing or counter submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation deed, pay the registration fee and matrícula mercantil, and file the Registro Único Empresarial form. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal evidencing legal personality, the company's NIT pre-assignment, and the legal representative's powers.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation deed
Pre-approved name certificate
Legal representative's identification and acceptance of office
Shareholders' identification documents
Completed RUES registration form
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the corporate purpose's compatibility with professional services or regulatory consultancy (which is unrestricted under ISIC 7490), the applicant submits a written clarification and, if necessary, amends the corporate purpose clause and refiles; no sanctions accrue for a first query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN and NIT Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (online via RUES-integrated RUT application or DIAN web portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) application, obtain the NIT, and register the responsible economic activities (CIIU 7490), principal tax obligations (income tax, VAT for taxable services, ICA complementary), and the electronic invoicing authorization. The legal representative must accept the NIT electronically.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Legal representative's citizenship card or passport
Shareholders' identification data
Corporate purpose description
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT application is rejected due to data inconsistency or missing mandatory fields, the legal representative corrects the information and resubmits online; DIAN typically resolves the recurrence within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the company registration certificate, NIT/RUT, first board resolution, and legal representative identification to the chosen bank. Open the corporate checking account, deposit the subscribed cash capital (if applicable), and obtain the bank certificate evidencing the paid-up capital position.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (issued within 90 days)
RUT with NIT
First board resolution appointing the legal representative
Legal representative's identification document
Beneficial ownership and PEP declaration forms
Proof of corporate address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional due diligence on the beneficial owner, the entity submits the sworn beneficial-ownership structure and the shareholders' identification; the bank clears the account typically within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Fire Safety and Labor Registration for the Physical Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá (Secretaría Distrital de Planeación en conjunto con el Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos) and ARL occupational risk insurer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo (zoning certificate) for the office address, secure the fire-safety inspection certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) for the leased premises, and register the company with the occupational risk administrator (ARL) and social security entities prior to hiring personnel. File the Industria y Comercio (ICA) activity declaration with the district revenue office.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Certificate of zoning usage from the planning authority
Building fire-safety inspection report
RUT and NIT
Company payroll and worker registration forms (once hiring commences)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning certification is denied, the company may apply to relocate to a compatible commercial location and request the visa of a new certificate; if the fire-safety inspection reveals deficiencies, corrective measures are implemented and a re-inspection is requested within ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing license is required; the entity performs professional regulatory consulting services only (ISIC 7490, NAICS 541690), which are unrestricted professional activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no sectoral operating permit is mandated for FDA/CE regulatory consulting; only a municipal zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) and a commercial establishment registration with the Chamber of Commerce are required for the physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (Bogotá District Environment Secretariat) — applicable only if the office operations generate non-domestic discharges; otherwise no environmental agency intervention is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is office-based and generates no industrial emissions, process wastewater, or VOC discharges; there is no EIA report, registration, or environmental license requirement under Colombian Law 99 of 1993 and Decree 1076 of 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — only ordinary domestic sanitary and solid-waste disposal standards apply, aligned with municipal wastewater utility thresholds and Resolution 0631 of 2015 domestic discharge limits; no industrial effluent or air emission permit is triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (Certificado de Bomberos) obtained through the official fire brigade inspection of the office premises; structural load and electrical installation verification by the property landlord or municipal civil defense, as required by local building code; occupational health and safety clearance through enrollment in a licensed ARL with a risk classification suited to professional desk-based activities; mandatory and complete social-security registry prior to the start of any personnel activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — official portal: www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities without a legal presence in Colombia must appoint a local fiscal agent or legal representative, execute a power of attorney before a notary, obtain a specific tax residence certificate, and apply for NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through DIAN’s cleartax / Muisca portal. The application requires corporate documentation apostillized and translated into Spanish, financial statements, and identification of the effective beneficial owner. Upon approval, DIAN issues a NIT with a unique 11-digit code, valid indefinitely, and the taxpayer must be registered in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT), which constitutes the single statutory tax ID for all VAT, income tax, and customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombian law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through regime. A Colombian S.A.S. is an entity-level taxpayer subject to national corporate income tax on worldwide income. No deemed partnership election is allowed for domestic purposes; hybrid mismatch elections may be analyzed by treaty partners, but the default Colombian classification is a taxable corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Colombian VAT registration is mandatory without a local threshold for foreign entities that have a permanent establishment, perform taxable events in Colombia, or sell digital services. For domestic SMEs, the simplified regime applies to taxpayers with annual gross income of up to COP 3,500 per million; however, a foreign MedTech regulatory consulting company exporting services will require VAT registration only if it has Colombian customers or performs taxable activities within Colombia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia mandates real-time electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) for all VAT-registered taxpayers through DIAN. The electronic invoice must be issued via an authorized software provider using the factura electrónica de venta (FEV) format, signed with a DIAN-issued digital certificate, and validated telematically before delivery to the purchaser or the receipt is sent within 48 hours. For each invoice, the supplier must transmit the XML to DIAN over the webservice API, receive a validation response, and stamp the electronic invoice. There is no separate excise-stamping regime; compliance is achieved exclusively through the telematic clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Colombian taxpayer may apply a 0% VAT rate only for (i) tangible goods physically exported from Colombian customs territory, evidenced by a valid single export declaration (Declaración de Exportación), or (ii) services rendered exclusively to a foreign recipient and effectively used or exploited outside Colombia, as specified under Articles 481 and the complementary provisions of the Colombian Tax Code. Consulting, advisory, and regulatory compliance services performed for foreign medical device manufacturers are zero-rated if the results are delivered to a nonresident customer, the intellectual property and economic utilization of the service is realized abroad, and the invoice is issued to a foreign commercial domicile.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Apostilled commercial contract with export intention
Electronic single export declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DEX)
Certified bill of lading (or air-freight airway bill, where applicable)
Customs exit stamp and security manifestation
Bank automatic exchange-rate certification for foreign currency inflow
Inward remittance certificate (Certificado de Negociación de Divisas) issued by the Colombian intermediary bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to forward and backward audit scrutiny by DIAN. The taxpayer must prove actual physical export or offshore provision; for intangible services, the burden includes templates, service deliverables, and communication logs to prove extraterritorial use. If export documentation is incomplete, falsified, or the foreign exchange is not repatriated within 180 calendar days, DIAN will retroactively claw back the full IVA not collected, apply statutory interest (1.5 times the current usury rate), impose a penalty equal to 100% of the omitted tax under Article 648 of the Tax Code, and may initiate criminal proceedings for tax fraud when documents are falsified, with prison sentences of up to 9 years in aggravated cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), operating jointly with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for the administration of the international exchange regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a regulated liberalized convertibility regime under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, Decree 2245 of 2015 and circulars of the Banco de la República. Current-account transactions (imports, exports, services, interest, dividends) are freely convertible but are subject to mandatory declaración de cambio through authorized intermediaries. Capital-account transactions, foreign direct investment (FDI), portfolio investment and external credit, require registration in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (RII) of the Banco de la República. Dividend and profit remittance for a duly registered S.A.S. is permitted without prior administrative authorization, provided the income has been recognized in audited financial statements and the local withholding tax on dividends (currently 5% for resident entities, 10% as a treaty minimum in certain holding structures) has been settled. Remittance impediments arise principally from unregistered FDI, incomplete RII disclosures, unresolved tax liens, or failure to present the Formulario de Declaración de Cambio prior to the outflow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exporters must channel 100% of the FOB value of export proceeds through the Colombian foreign exchange market, through an authorized bank, financial corporation or exchange house, within six months from the date of export registration; the Banco de la República may extend, restrict or individualize this term in line with Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83. De minimis operations equal to or below USD 10,000 per individual export event are exempt from mandatory channeling. For service exports the channeling period is generally six months and the threshold is USD 50,000 aggregate per calendar month. Natural persons and services exporters must surrender exports of services via declaración de cambio; there is no fractional surrender ratio applicable to standard S.A.S. exporters, so the effective conversion ratio is 100% for canalizable receipts. Non-channelized proceeds are treated as a foreign-exchange infraction and expose the exporter to fines issued by DIAN and restrictions on subsequent exchange operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (COP/dual-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (COP/dual-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Foreign Investment Proceeds Sub-Account
Operational Account with International Clearing Module
Operational Account and Restricted FX Compliance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Mercury, N26 and similar do not hold Colombian banking licenses and cannot serve as vehicles for exchange declarations, statutory capital escrow, RII registration, or profit-remittance corroboration. Their practical utility is restricted to satellite or contingency clearing for non-regulated low-value disbursements (subcontractor fees, cloud software licensing, tokenized R&D expenses) if the supporting service contract and VAT invoice are produced. Using an EMI as the principal treasury rail without a Colombian exchange declaration poses a substantial regulatory risk of un-channelized currency under the régimen cambiario and can be challenged during AML/KYC due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Circular Básica Jurídica and bank internal onboarding policies, at least one Colombian resident legal representative (representante legal) must attend a face-to-face interview at the bank branch or before a certified officer, presenting the original cédula de ciudadanía. Remote onboarding may be permitted by certain tier-1 banks via a live video call with identity verification, but the final branch approval almost always requires apostilled board resolutions, the Colombian Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Cámara de Comercio), the RUT, and an original power of attorney if the foreign founder will operate the account. Non-resident directors do not need to travel if a formal power of attorney, apostilled and translated into Spanish, is granted to the Colombian legal representative. Onboarding viability therefore depends on prompt local representation rather than physical presence of every director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible professional services invoice without a granular description of FDA/CE milestones, causing ambiguity between consulting fees and technology-transfer royalties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master services agreement and per-project statements of work with deliverables, milestone acceptance reports signed by the client, laboratory/prototype documentation as relevant, itemized timesheets of specialist consultants, senior-staff CVs, and invoices cross-referenced to project names and fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder holding an intermediate entity in a low-tax or offshore jurisdiction, generating enhanced due-diligence review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate organizational chart to ultimate beneficial owners, apostilled certificate of incumbency and good standing from the intermediate jurisdiction, RUT and Cámara de Comercio certificate, sworn declarations for source of wealth of each UBO, audited financial statements of the intermediate entity and the S.A.S., and a local Colombian substance plan (office, staff or active documentation of consulting operations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of funds received through offshore EMI rails with rapid onward disbursement, resembling layering or structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy, client settlements to service level agreements, a secure payment record mapping each EMI inflow to approved invoices, logical accumulation stages with accounting entries, Form 110 annual income tax return demonstrating revenue recognition, and a 12-month look-back of bank statements to evidence legitimate operational cash-flow rhythm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound remittances exceeding USD 10,000 per event without full commercial-paper reconciliations, especially if the declared purpose code is inconsistent with bank activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed invoices, supplier contracts, exchange declarations (Formulario de Declaración de Cambio), intercompany transfer pricing documentation (TPD) if applicable, tax identification data of the recipients, evidence that Colombian withholding and VAT (IVA) rules were observed, and a certificate of good tax standing (paz y salvo) where required by the intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a foreign equity contribution to the S.A.S., the remitter executes an SWIFT MT103 transfer to the company's COP or USD account (if dual-currency authorized) at a Colombian commercial bank, quoting the company NIT and the payment reference 'Aporte de capital / FDI registration'. Prior to receipt, the company must present to the intermediary bank the pro-forma registrational dossier: board resolution approving the investment, updated bylaws, RUT certificate, identification of each shareholder, and the bank's own foreign-investment questionnaire. The intermediary bank then prepares and files the Declaración de Cambio using the standard capital-account purpose code for direct foreign investment and submits the registration to the Banco de la República's RII system within the statutory deadline. Registration in RII is mandatory to authorize future profit repatriation and capital liquidation dividends. Funds arriving without these supporting instruments may be rejected under anti-corruption and cross-border inbound-risk controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the S.A.S. are (i) SWIFT MT103 for service invoices, software license royalties, contractor payments and tax/social-security disbursements; (ii) domestic ACH (Cenit operated by ACH Colombia) for local Colombian peso payments; and (iii) corporate commercial letters of credit exclusively for physical equipment purchases, issued via MT700 and confirmed with transport and inspection documents. For every outbound foreign-exchange operation equal to or above the de minimis threshold, the bank must receive a declaración de cambio with the appropriate import-of-services purpose code, supported by the service contract, invoice, and, where applicable, transfer pricing policy. Use of a commercial LC for pure MedTech consulting is atypical and should be limited to a client requirement; the company should rely on SWIFT/ACH as the cost-effective statutory-compliant rails. Treasury must also retain payment evidence such as an MT103 with the Colombia NIT, applicant and beneficiary names, and invoicing references for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards on USD/COP contracted with authorized Colombian commercial banks with a documented hedge intent and matching cash-flow forecast.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/COP through licensed Colombian intermediaries or recognized cross-border dealers, using the reference rate published by the Banco de la República.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) converting USD SOFR floating debt-service into COP fixed-rate obligations for bank-approved external debt.
USD/COP vanilla FX options executed with an earmarked premium and limited stated maximum loss, allowed solely as a hedging overlay for exported service receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual commercial registry renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge of COP 20,000 to 200,000 plus monthly interest penalties; continued non-renewal for more than one year exposes the SAS to fines and administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April-May of the following fiscal year according to the DIAN tax calendar, based on the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to 5% of total tax owing, capped at 1,000 UVT, plus daily interest; failure to file may trigger DIAN's automatic assessment and freeze of bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline generally in May-June of the following fiscal year, per DIAN annual schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit by the deadline incurs fines of up to 5% of the information value; late reports are treated as a substantive violation and may attract daily late-filing penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered domicile (integrated with the annual chamber renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil, on or before 31 March each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance can block the issuance of the certificate of existence and representation and subject the SAS to fines under the AML framework; ongoing failure may lead to administrative suspension.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) is required when a SAS's gross assets at year-end exceed 5,000 current minimum monthly wages (SMMLV) or gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV; it is also required if the entity is listed, exercises public activity, or the bylaws expressly mandate it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Generally Accepted Accounting Standards (NIIF/IFRS for Colombia) apply: full NIIF for Group 1 entities and NIIF for PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for most SAS consulting entities; micro-business standards apply only to qualifying micro SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the annual Chamber renewal, the legal representative must confirm and update the list of direct and ultimate beneficial owners holding 5% or more of capital or control. Share transfers occurring during the year must be reflected in the internal share register and reported through the RUB declaration submitted with the commercial renewal by 31 March.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general corporate income tax rate applicable to Colombian S.A.S. for taxable years 2022 onwards)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; limited deductions available for investments in technological innovation (50% deduction under Law 1955/2019) and for certain creative/software activities; no preferential rate for regulatory consulting services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return), filed electronically via DIAN portal (MUISCA system at www.dian.gov.co)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline is assigned based on the last digit of the taxpayer’s NIT (tax ID) for the fiscal year end; generally falls between April and May of the following fiscal year. For tax year 2024, the filing window runs from April 9 through May 12, 2025.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income net of returns, rebates, and discounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Colombian-source gross income attributable to the S.A.S.; exclude foreign source income not taxable in Colombia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute after applying allowable deductions, including expenses directly related to FDA/CE compliance consulting activities; ensure transfer pricing adjustments are reflected if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income tax payable (35% of net taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply withholding tax credits and any advance payments; non-resident shareholders may not take credit for expenses not related to Colombian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due per each month or partial month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due; if no tax due, penalty equal to 0.5% of gross income up to a maximum of COP 3,000 normalized units (UVT); additionally, daily interest accrues at the statutory rate (Art. 641 and 649 Tax Statute).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders when the distributed profits have been subject to Colombian corporate income tax at the entity level; no additional national taxation at the shareholder level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding rate under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) submit the TRC and a letter of adhesion to the Colombian withholding agent prior to the payment; (3) ensure the beneficial owner is qualified under the treaty’s limitation-of-benefits provision; (4) the withholding agent must file Form 468 through DIAN to register the reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates on payments to non-residents: 15% for royalties (including license fees for IP) and 15% for debt interest. Applicable DTA may reduce rates (e.g., 5-10% for interest on financial institutions and 5-10% for royalties under withdrawal of DTA protocols); relevant treaty documentation must be filed each calendar year.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing return (Form 120) and supporting documentation (Local File and Master File) required when taxpayer's gross income reaches or exceeds 135,000 UVT (approx. COP 6.3 billion for 2025) or when total equity or gross net worth is equal to or greater than 70,000 UVT AND related-party transactions exceed 45,000 UVT (approx. COP 2.1 billion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime for ordinary operating companies; however, general anti-avoidance provisions (Art. 869 Tax Statute) and CFC rules require that the S.A.S. maintain substantive commercial operations, physical or virtual presence, and a legitimate business purpose to support treaty benefits and avoid denial of deductions or recharacterization of transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing Formulario 210 with inflated deductible expenses or omitted Colombian-source income, including understating service fees from global regulatory consulting engagements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalty under Article 434B of the Colombian Tax Statute: imprisonment of 5 to 9 years and a fine of 200% of the evaded amount. Additionally, civil tax settlements may impose penalty of up to 200% of the omitted income and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt if they participated in the fraud or failed to exercise due diligence; personal assets may be seized, travel bans imposed, and criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. as a passive conduit that subcontracts all substantive work to related offshore parties while claiming Colombian management fees or treaty benefits without local decision-making or operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of anti-abuse rules may cause full disallowance of deductible payments, reassessment of income at the hands of the Colombian entity, and penalty of up to 200% of the omitted tax; the DIAN may also cancel the NIT and statute-limitation periods remain open indefinitely.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the entire reassessed tax and penalties under liability-shifting rules (Art. 794 Tax Statute); in addition, a declaration of a sham company allows creditors and the tax authority to pierce the corporate veil and seek recovery from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting wire transfers or credit card payments from clients without implementing sufficient client due diligence, or failing to report suspicious transactions to Colombia’s Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF) when engaged in physically cross-border advisory services or invoicing through high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 526/1999 and external regulation 2018 per UIAF guidelines: up to 1,000 current legal monthly minimum wages (approx. COP 1.3 billion) for financial reporting breaches; criminal money-laundering charges under Article 323 of the Criminal Code carry imprisonment of 10 to 30 years for directing or through negligence allowing laundering of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally accountable for the entity’s AML compliance deficiencies; they may be fined individually, prohibited from leaving the country, and subject to criminal indictment for the failure to prevent laundering activities, including extradition in serious cross-border cases.
